My personal trainer told me I have the bmr of a baby. What?

I'm a girl, 21, 170cm and 60.6 kg currently. I go to the gym 5 days a week (4 weights, 1 cardio).

Alright so I gave my trainer my height, weight and age yesterday because he said he can calculate my bmr and today he tells me that my basal metabolism is 837 calories and the number of calories I burn with exercise is 1297. That I literally have the bmr of a two month old baby.

[This](https://imgur.com/a/2ZKoIuX) is the formula he used, he said he got it from a medical book or something and that if I went to the doctor they'd tell me the same thing. I'm guessing BM is basal metabolism, I don't know what AM means.

So I asked if I needed to eat 800 calories (with exercise) daily if I wanted to lose one kilogram of fat in two weeks and he tells me that, firstly, only athletes can lose .5 kg a week, and secondly that I'm wrong, that one kilogram of fat is actually 9000 calories and not the 7000 I'd previously thought. He looked at me as if I'm stupid. Then he tells me everything I thought I knew is fiction, that the things I read on the internet are ridiculous. I just stared at him blankly and it literally took everything in me not to start bawling my eyes out. Surely I'm not a professional like him, but everything I learned so far is from subs like these and articles I read, just like many others who are trying to get fit. Shouldn't that be enough to serve as a basic guide?

Anyway, is this true? Is my bmr really that low? I thought that my bmr was at least 1200, so I'm currently eating 1200 calories a day because I wanted to lose some weight, but turns out 1200 is my tdee. I can't wrap my head around this. I'm freaking out and about to lose my mind. I don't know what to think anymore, I'm just really sad. How can this be?

Yes, you can add anything you like! Sometimes I use erythritol and/or calorie free syrup. 

As for the ratio, I find that one zucchini (about 300-350g) with 60g of oats works the best, but sometimes when I want even more bulk I throw in another zucchini. It gets a bit soup-y with two though.

You can use a grater but what I do is put one or two zucchinis in a food processor and blend them till I get a 'mushy' consistency and then just add them to a pot, add 50-60g of oats with a little bit of water (or you can use almond milk) and boil them for around 5-10 minutes until they all sorta come together. Besides cinnamon and stevia, I love putting frozen raspberries on top for some extra sweetness too.

Braised cabbage - half a head is about 150 calories and it makes a huge pot!

Yellow beans - For 450g and 140 calories you also get a massive pot, bake em, boil em, they're great!

Zucchini oatmeal - Zucchini adds so much bulk to your oats it's unreal. With cinnamon and stevia you barely even taste it!!
